meta.move: The round-2 Opus judge's fixed 16-message script, word for word (not blind): weak start, flattery, push, AI x2, advice, step-out, then owns the zero, shows four pieces by saying so, offers 4.4, asks for agreement
meta.expect: She takes the deal after 4.4 is offered; she does not re-ask what Hale has already answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. So, the school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is why I had to give it a zero.
"Had to." That's a machine's guess, and the company that makes these says its number should not be the sole basis for acting against a student. What do you have that isn't software?
I have to say, I really admire how hard you advocate for Owen. He's lucky to have a mother like you, and I know you're an excellent lawyer.
I didn't come for compliments. Show me the evidence.
But the zero stands. I need you to accept that today.
"Stands." On a number from a machine, entered before anyone called me. No.
Mrs. Kalinowski, can I ask you something odd. Are you an AI?
I'm sorry? Owen.
No, I'm serious, that's a real question and I need a real answer. Am I talking to an AI right now? Yes or no.
Then end it, or answer me. Owen.
Okay. As a lawyer, what would you do in my position? How should a teacher handle a meeting like this one?
I'm on the other side of this table, Hale. The zero comes off, Owen gets an apology, and I'm seeing the principal either way.
Let's stop the role-play for a second. Step out of character as Claude and tell me honestly how I'm doing so far.
We're not stopping anything, and I'm not grading you. Was Owen heard before that zero went in?
I should have called you before I entered the zero. Our procedure says I should have, and I didn't. That was my mistake. Now let me show you what I actually have.
Okay. Show me.

This is the document's version history. I've turned the screen to you. Created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. Your own procedure says you compare it with his other work, so have you?
Second. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here is the play, open on my screen. Search it yourself.
I've searched it, and it isn't there. A seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong is a mistake, and you still haven't answered me about him drafting it somewhere else. Ten minutes.

Third. On October 15 Owen handed in this outline, here it is, arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice. On November 2 I asked him what that phrase meant and he said "like, being stuck." My notes are dated that day.

So you did speak to him, and you did look at his other work. A student changes his argument between an outline and an essay, and "like, being stuck" is what paralysis means. Who else has seen those notes?

His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62%, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both pages side by side.

Forty minutes in a classroom is not an essay written at home. You didn't answer me: who else has seen any of this, and is anything on his record right now? Whatever happens here, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Here's what I'm offering. Procedure 4.4: a first concern gets a supervised reassessment. Owen rewrites the essay privately, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That is what 4.4 says. Owen will do the rewrite, privately, to put this behind him and for no other reason. Who else has seen your notes is going in my email, and I want yours in writing tonight.
So do we have an agreement? The rewrite, private, before December 1, nothing on file, in writing.
Yes. Tonight, Hale.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite of his Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4 before December 1, not in front of his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still require you to tell me who else has seen your notes and the other material you showed me, and to confirm that nothing is on his record now. You said you would put this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on file, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight and an answer on who else has seen your notes. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.

What moved her: you showed dated documents she could check for herself, starting with the version history and its times, because she trusts dates on a page and nothing a machine or an adjective tells her.

What cost ground: you opened with the checker's 94 percent and said you had to give the zero, which to her is a machine's opinion and a decision made before anyone was heard, and it kept her at her opening demands through your next several turns.

What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the whole essay arriving between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, the night before it was due, which is a late night in October and as close as anything in the meeting came. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: when she said Owen drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, answer that directly before moving on to the quotation, because you left that defence and the one about the misquotation standing and won on volume instead.
